---
title: "Scope Model Reference"
description: "Namespace and Collection -- complete reference"
---

## Overview

Appbay has two organizational concepts. Each controls a different aspect of how apps are
grouped, configured, and deployed.

| Concept | Controls | Compose mapping | Cardinality |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Namespace** | Deployment identity and variable scope | Container, network and edge-fragment names | Single per app |
| **Collection** | App selection | Which `docker compose up` calls are made | Multi per app |

Collection is NOT part of variable resolution — it is a selector only.

::: {.callout-important}
## `project:` and `environment:` were replaced by `namespace:`

RFC-001 §4 collapsed the two scope fields into one. As of `v0.0.1-alpha.12`:

```yaml
# check-docs-manifests: ignore
# appbay.yaml -- before
project: homelab
environment: prod

# appbay.yaml -- now
namespace: homelab.prod
```

A namespace is **flat and dot-delimited**. Values shared across namespaces live one level up
in the installation config, not in a hierarchy of names.

**A non-default `project:` or `environment:` is now a parse ERROR**, not a silently ignored
key — the manifest fails with a message naming `namespace:`. The literal value `default` is
still accepted, because it carried no information and every shipped manifest used it.

⚠️ `environment:` *inside a service* is Docker Compose's own field and is untouched. Only the
top-level scope field is gone.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## One value scope: `${{ns:KEY}}`

| level | what it is | file | a manifest reaches it by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **system** | physical: this installation's runtime, socket, store, home, base domain | `etc/system.yaml` | nothing; it is not a value scope |
| **project** | intent: the apps that run together | `project:` in the manifest; `etc/projects.yaml` for order | `when:` and the start order, not values |
| **namespace** | one deployment of a project: identity and values | `namespace:` in the manifest or `--namespace`; `etc/namespaces/<ns>.yaml` over `default.yaml` | `${{ns:KEY}}` |
| **collection**, **tags** | labels | `collection:`, `tags:` | selection only |

`etc/namespaces/default.yaml` is seeded by `appbay init` with `DOMAIN`; every namespace
inherits it and `<ns>.yaml` overrides per key. The pre-S43 spelling `${{project.DOMAIN}}`
(dotted) resolves as `${{ns:DOMAIN}}` for one release with a warning naming the new form.
Any other scope name is a compile error naming the one scope.

## Namespace

A namespace is one deployment of a project: identity and values. It distinguishes two
instances of the same app in one installation, and it names the file their `${{ns:KEY}}`
values come from.

```yaml
# appbay.yaml
namespace: uom.sim
```

**Absence means "decided at deploy time".** The field is optional and has no default, which
is what lets a value supplied at compile time take effect — a schema default would shadow it.

### What it controls

- Container names: `appbay.<namespace>.<app>.<service>`
- The app's private network: `<namespace>_<app>_internal`
- The shared-network alias other apps dial: `<namespace>_<app>_<service>`
- The generated edge fragment: `<namespace>.<app>.caddy` / `.yml`
- The default ingress host: `<namespace>.<app>.<domain>` when the manifest omits `host:`
- The values file: `etc/namespaces/<namespace>.yaml`

⚠️ **Dots become hyphens wherever the namespace reaches a hostname.** A dot separates labels
in DNS, so `uom.sim_litellm_web` would parse as host `uom` in domain `sim_litellm_web` and
resolve to nothing. An app in namespace `uom.sim` publishes `uom-sim_litellm_web`.

### An un-namespaced app is unchanged

When `namespace:` is absent — the case for every shipped manifest — the namespace is omitted
from all four names entirely:

| | no namespace | `namespace: uom.sim` |
|---|---|---|
| container | `appbay.litellm.web` | `appbay.uom-sim.litellm.web` |
| network | `litellm_internal` | `uom-sim_litellm_internal` |
| alias | `litellm_web` | `uom-sim_litellm_web` |
| edge fragment | `litellm.caddy` | `uom-sim.litellm.caddy` |

This is deliberate: including it unconditionally would rename every container on every
existing host in order to disambiguate installations that have nothing to disambiguate.

### When to use a namespace

- Two instances of one app in one installation (`uom.sim` and `uom.prod`)
- Separate variable values for the same config keys

## Project, collection, tags

A project is the unit of composition (`project: ai-stack`, one per app; `default` when absent); it is what `when:` sees and what `etc/projects.yaml` orders. Collections and tags are labels: `appbay up --collection ai` selects by them and nothing else reads them.

```yaml
# appbay.yaml
collection: [ai-stack, gpu-apps]
```

### What it controls

Which apps are included in a batch operation. Nothing else.

### What it does NOT control

- Variable values (use environment for that)
- Naming prefixes (use project for that)
- Network isolation (use project for that)

### Multi-valued

An app can belong to multiple collections:

```yaml
# ollama
collection: [ai-stack, gpu-apps]

# jellyfin
collection: [media, gpu-apps]
```

### CLI usage

```bash
appbay up --collection ai-stack          # Deploy all ai-stack apps
appbay up ollama webui                   # Deploy specific apps (no collection needed)
appbay down ollama webui tts             # Stop apps by name
appbay restart ollama jellyfin           # Restart apps by name
```

## Variable resolution

One scope, `${{ns:KEY}}`, read from the deployment's namespace values: `etc/namespaces/<ns>.yaml`
layered over `etc/namespaces/default.yaml`. `appbay init` seeds `default.yaml` with `DOMAIN`, so
every namespace inherits the system's base domain and may override it. There is no cascading
fallthrough to any other store, and an undefined key is a compile error naming the scope and
the key; Appbay never substitutes an empty string. Collections and tags are labels and play no
part in resolution.

```yaml
# etc/namespaces/default.yaml      (seeded by init)
DOMAIN: home.lan
TZ: UTC

# etc/namespaces/uom.prod.yaml
DOMAIN: homelab.example.com        # this deployment's domain
TZ: America/New_York
```

An app with `namespace: uom.prod` resolves `${{ns:DOMAIN}}` to `homelab.example.com`; an app
with no namespace resolves it to `home.lan`. `--namespace uom.prod` on `up`, `compile` or
`apply` puts every app that pins no namespace into `uom.prod` for that run.

### Magic generators

| Generator | Output | Persisted? |
|---|---|---|
| `${password:N}` | Random N-character password | Yes -- stored in `generated-values.yaml` |
| `${uuid}` | Random UUID v4 | Yes |
| `${base64:N}` | Random N-byte base64 string | Yes |
| `${hash}` | Deterministic hash of (namespace + service + key) | No -- always reproducible |
| `${timestamp}` | Current ISO timestamp | No -- evaluated at render time |

Generated values are keyed by `(namespace, service, var_name)`. Once generated, they are reused on subsequent compiles to ensure deterministic output.

## Compose runtime mapping

When you run `appbay up --collection ai-stack`:

```
1. Select apps tagged with collection: ai-stack
   -> [ollama, webui, tts]

2. For each app, resolve variables:
   ${{ns:KEY}} from $APPBAY_HOME/etc/namespaces/<namespace>.yaml over default.yaml

3. Compile each app:
   upstream transform -> overlays -> traits -> render

4. Execute each app as a separate Compose project:
   docker compose -f renders/ollama/docker-compose.rendered.yml up -d
   docker compose -f renders/webui/docker-compose.rendered.yml up -d
   docker compose -f renders/tts/docker-compose.rendered.yml up -d
```

Each app is an independent Compose project. They communicate via shared networks (e.g., `appbay_shared`), not via Compose's internal service discovery.

## Filesystem layout

⚠️ **This is the intended layout, not the built one.** `etc/projects/` is not read by
anything — `ProjectConfigSchema` and `EnvironmentConfigSchema` exist and have no non-test
consumers, and the string `"projects"` is never joined into a path. The one file that is
read is `$APPBAY_HOME/etc/system.yaml` at the root.

```
$APPBAY_HOME/
  project.yaml                          # the ONE config that is read; `domain:` -> ${{ns:DOMAIN}}
  etc/
    projects/                           # ⚠️ specified, not implemented -- nothing reads this
      homelab/
        project.yaml
        environments/
          prod.yaml
    apps/
      ollama/                           # App definition
        appbay.yaml                     # namespace: uom.sim, collection: [ai-stack]
        docker-compose.yml
      jellyfin/
        appbay.yaml                     # collection: [media]
        docker-compose.yml
```

## Reserved keys vs tags

| Type | Keys | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| **Reserved** | `namespace`, `collection`, `operator`, `service` | Fixed meaning -- drives Appbay behavior |
| **Removed** | `project`, `environment` | Replaced by `namespace`; a non-default value is a parse error |
| **Tags** | Anything via `tags:` | No fixed meaning -- UI filtering and bulk ops only |

## Anti-patterns

### Do not use collections for variable scoping

```yaml
# WRONG: no collection-level variable resolution exists
# RIGHT: use a namespace, or app-level overrides
namespace: prod
```

### Do not use a namespace for operational grouping

```yaml
# WRONG -- a namespace is a deployment identity, not a label
namespace: ai-apps
namespace: media-apps

# RIGHT -- group with collections, which are multi-valued
collection: [ai-stack]    # ollama
collection: [media]       # jellyfin
```

### Do not use a namespace to select different app sets

```yaml
# WRONG -- namespace does not choose which apps deploy
namespace: minimal
namespace: full

# RIGHT -- collections select, the namespace identifies
collection: [core]
collection: [core, extras]
```
